note: The ONLY actions Laptop Guardian can execute. Single source of truth for the bridge (planning, UI text) and PowerShell (parameter validation, admin enforcement). AI output never adds to or alters this list.

actions.label: Stop process
actions.summary: Asks Windows to end process {name} (PID {pid}). Guardian first re-checks that this PID is still the same program, started at the same time, from the same path.
actions.consequences: Unsaved work in that program is lost. If a startup entry, scheduled task or service relaunches it, it comes back; use Disable restart to stop that.
actions.undo: Not reversible. Start the program again yourself if you need it.

actions.label: Disable restart
actions.summary: Turns off the startup entry '{name}' at {location} using Windows' own startup-approval flag (the same switch as Settings > Apps > Startup). Nothing is deleted.
actions.consequences: The program stops starting automatically at sign-in. It stays installed and you can still start it by hand.
actions.undo: Use Re-enable restart on the Action Center history, or switch it back on in Settings > Apps > Startup.

actions.label: Re-enable restart
actions.summary: Turns the startup entry '{name}' at {location} back on (clears its disabled flag).
actions.consequences: The program starts automatically at the next sign-in again.
actions.undo: Disable restart again.

actions.label: Disable scheduled task
actions.summary: Disables the scheduled task {taskPath}{taskName} in Task Scheduler. The task definition is kept.
actions.consequences: The task no longer runs on its schedule or triggers. Whatever it maintained (updates, sync) stops until you re-enable it.
actions.undo: Re-enable scheduled task from the Action Center history, or in Task Scheduler.

actions.label: Re-enable scheduled task
actions.summary: Enables the scheduled task {taskPath}{taskName} again.
actions.consequences: The task runs on its triggers again.
actions.undo: Disable scheduled task again.

actions.label: Disable service
actions.summary: Sets the Windows service {name} to Disabled (it will not start at boot). Guardian records its previous start type so it can be restored. The running instance is not stopped.
actions.consequences: The service will not start again after it stops or after a restart. Programs that depend on it may stop working until it is re-enabled.
actions.undo: Re-enable service restores the previous start type.

actions.label: Re-enable service
actions.summary: Restores the start type of service {name}.
actions.consequences: The service can start again.
actions.undo: Disable service again.

actions.label: Recycle file
actions.summary: Moves the single file {path} to the Recycle Bin. It is not permanently deleted.
actions.consequences: The file disappears from its folder and counts toward the Recycle Bin until you empty it. Programs that expect it there may stop working.
actions.undo: Open the Recycle Bin, right-click the file and choose Restore.

actions.label: Update now
actions.summary: Runs Microsoft Defender's own signature update (Update-MpSignature).
actions.consequences: Downloads the latest definitions from Microsoft. No files on your laptop are changed.
actions.undo: Nothing to undo.

actions.label: Run quick scan now
actions.summary: Starts a Microsoft Defender quick scan (Start-MpScan -ScanType QuickScan) and waits for it to finish.
actions.consequences: Uses CPU and disk for a few minutes. Defender handles anything it finds using its normal rules.
actions.undo: Nothing to undo.

actions.label: Run integrity check now
actions.summary: Runs two read-only Windows checks: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth and sfc /verifyonly. Neither repairs anything.
actions.consequences: Takes several minutes and uses disk and CPU. It only reports; fixing problems is a separate, manual step.
actions.undo: Nothing to undo.

actions.label: Enable firewall now
actions.summary: Turns Windows Defender Firewall ON for the {profile} profile (Set-NetFirewallProfile -Enabled True). Guardian never turns it off.
actions.consequences: Windows blocks unsolicited inbound connections for that profile again, according to your existing rules.
actions.undo: Re-enabling is safe; turning the firewall off is only possible in Windows Security.

actions.label: Flush DNS cache
actions.summary: Clears the Windows DNS resolver cache (Clear-DnsClientCache).
actions.consequences: The next lookup of each site asks your DNS server again, which can be a little slower once. Fixes stale or wrong cached addresses.
actions.undo: Nothing to undo; the cache refills by itself.

actions.label: Uninstall cleanly with Revo
actions.summary: Opens Revo Uninstaller (its own window) for you to uninstall {appName}. Guardian does not uninstall anything itself and will only report success after it can verify the app is gone.
actions.consequences: Revo shows its own prompts and removes the program and leftovers according to your choices there. Unsaved work in the app is lost.
actions.undo: Reinstall the application if you remove it by mistake. Revo can create a restore point first; enable that in Revo.

actions.label: Repair schedule
actions.summary: Re-registers Guardian's own Daily, Weekly and Dashboard scheduled tasks from your Settings.
actions.consequences: Fixes tasks that drifted from Settings or lack the scheduled-run marker. Elevated tasks are never downgraded; changing them asks Windows for permission.
actions.undo: Change the schedule in Settings and save again.

actions.label: Block program
actions.summary: Creates ONE Windows Firewall rule in the "Laptop Guardian" group that blocks {direction} network traffic for the program {path}. Other rules are not touched.
actions.consequences: That program cannot use the network in that direction until you remove or disable the rule. Updates, sync or sign-in in that program may stop working.
actions.undo: Remove or disable the rule from Network Guard, Firewall (the rule is listed with its expiry).

actions.label: Allow program
actions.summary: Creates ONE Windows Firewall rule in the "Laptop Guardian" group that allows {direction} traffic for the reviewed program {path}.
actions.consequences: Windows lets that program through the firewall in that direction. Only allow programs you trust.
actions.undo: Remove or disable the rule from Network Guard, Firewall.

actions.label: Block port
actions.summary: Creates ONE Windows Firewall rule in the "Laptop Guardian" group that blocks INBOUND {protocol} connections to local port {port} from all profiles.
actions.consequences: Other computers can no longer reach whatever listens on that port. Local use on this laptop is not affected.
actions.undo: Remove or disable the rule from Network Guard, Firewall.

actions.label: Block address
actions.summary: Creates ONE Windows Firewall rule in the "Laptop Guardian" group that blocks OUTBOUND traffic to {remote} for every program.
actions.consequences: Nothing on this laptop can reach that address. Guardian refuses ranges that would cut off your gateway, DNS or DHCP server.
actions.undo: Remove or disable the rule from Network Guard, Firewall.

actions.label: Remove rule
actions.summary: Deletes the Laptop Guardian firewall rule {name}. Guardian refuses any rule that is not in its own group with its own name prefix.
actions.consequences: Traffic that the rule blocked or allowed is handled by the remaining firewall rules again.
actions.undo: Create the rule again from Network Guard if you want it back.

actions.label: Disable rule
actions.summary: Turns the Laptop Guardian firewall rule {name} off without deleting it.
actions.consequences: The rule stops having any effect until you enable it again.
actions.undo: Enable the rule again from Network Guard, Firewall.

actions.label: Enable rule
actions.summary: Turns the Laptop Guardian firewall rule {name} back on.
actions.consequences: The rule takes effect again.
actions.undo: Disable the rule again.

actions.label: Block domain
actions.summary: Adds "0.0.0.0 {domain}" inside the Laptop Guardian section of the Windows hosts file, so this exact host name stops resolving.
actions.consequences: Programs on this laptop cannot reach that name. Wildcards are not supported, and programs that use their own encrypted DNS (DoH) can bypass the hosts file. Needs DNS filtering to be switched on.
actions.undo: Unblock the domain, or roll back all DNS blocks, from Network Guard, DNS.

actions.label: Unblock domain
actions.summary: Removes {domain} from the Laptop Guardian section of the hosts file.
actions.consequences: The name resolves normally again once the DNS cache is flushed.
actions.undo: Block the domain again.

actions.label: Roll back all DNS blocks
actions.summary: Removes the whole Laptop Guardian section from the hosts file, restoring it to its text before Guardian added anything. Lines outside the section are never changed.
actions.consequences: Every domain Guardian blocked resolves normally again.
actions.undo: Block the domains again one by one if you want them back.

actions.label: Turn on DNS history log
actions.summary: Enables the Windows "DNS Client / Operational" event log so Deep Network Guard can show which program asked for which name. It records names only, never packets.
actions.consequences: Windows keeps a rolling record of DNS lookups on this laptop, which is private information. Turn it off when you are done.
actions.undo: Turn the DNS history log off from Network Guard, Deep mode.

actions.label: Turn off DNS history log
actions.summary: Disables the Windows "DNS Client / Operational" event log again.
actions.consequences: Windows stops recording DNS lookups in that log. Existing entries are not deleted.
actions.undo: Turn the DNS history log on again.

actions.label: Check that it is gone
actions.summary: Re-reads the installed-programs list and running processes to confirm {appName} is gone.
actions.consequences: Read-only.
actions.undo: Nothing to undo.
